title: Hodge classes realizing the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence
summary: Construct a coefficient-rational Hodge correspondence between equal-signature quaternionic Shimura varieties. The plan combines an explicit hermitian exterior-square comparison, harmonic theta classes with simultaneous sign nonvanishing, the unitary cohomological eigenspace calculation, and rational determinant descent. The all-prime Galois assertion retains Kottwitz’s conjecture as an explicit hypothesis. General Shimura, realization and theta machinery is imported from its owners; missing supplier interfaces are recorded precisely.
readme: Construct a coefficient-rational Hodge correspondence between equal-signature quaternionic Shimura varieties. The plan combines an explicit hermitian exterior-square comparison, harmonic theta classes with simultaneous sign nonvanishing, the unitary cohomological eigenspace calculation, and rational determinant descent. The all-prime Galois assertion retains Kottwitz’s conjecture as an explicit hypothesis. General Shimura, realization and theta machinery is imported from its owners; missing supplier interfaces are recorded precisely. The reader document specifies every target, convention, API and discriminating unit test. General automorphic cohomology, quaternionic Shimura foundations and theta identities belong to their existing suppliers and proposed Part II extensions.

stages.title: Quaternionic realizations and the correspondence target
stages.description: Targets: Jacquet–Langlands Hodge data: Fix a totally real field F of degree n, quaternion algebras B₁,B₂ with the same set Σ of split real places, d=|Σ|<n, and a cuspidal GL₂(A_F) representation π with trivial central character, even weights k_v≥2, and transfers π_i to B_i×. Put L=Q(π), containing Q(k). Use the unitary normalization r=0 and the coefficient representation τ_k=⊗_v Nrd_v^{(2−k_v)/2} Sym^{k_v−2}(τ_v), with its dual local system. F_Σ is the fixed field of automorphisms preserving Σ. An L-Hodge structure means a rational Hodge structure with L-action; equivalently use every embedding of L, rather than assuming conjugation preserves one arbitrary L-embedding. When d=0 use the finite compact Shimura set and its trivial-cocharacter constant model over Q; do not require Deligne’s exclusion of compact Q-adjoint factors for this degenerate case. The division-algebra reduction: For Jacquet–Langlands Hodge data, if B₁≅B₂ the identity on the multiplicity realization supplies the desired class through Poincaré duality. Otherwise the product Brauer class [B₁]+[B₂] has a quaternion division representative B. It is split at every real place, since B₁ and B₂ have identical real ramification. The theta construction below is used only in this second case. Quaternionic multiplicity realizations: For data as above let V_i be the L-rational π_i,f multiplicity space in H^d(Sh_{B_i},V_{k,i}). It is independent of sufficiently small level, has L-dimension 2^d, and is pure of weight d with this normalization. Its Betti and all étale realizations form an object of M_{F_Σ}^L. The self-dual coefficient pairing and Poincaré duality identify V_i with V_i∨(−d). The cohomological degree here is d, correcting the printed 2d on p. 19. Archimedean sign lines: For V_i of multiplicity-realization, its complexification decomposes into 2^d one-dimensional tensor sign lines indexed by signs at v∈Σ. At a split v the two cochain contributions have bidegrees (1,0) and (0,1); their actual coefficient-normalized Hodge types are (k_v/2,1−k_v/2) and the reversed pair. Outside Σ the degree-zero coefficient line contributes (0,0). Equal total Hodge types can have multiplicity, so retain the full tensor-sign indexing. The duality pairs opposite signs. The cohomological correspondence operator: Poincaré duality yields an L-linear identification V₁⊗_L V₂(d)≅Hom_L(V₁,V₂). On geometric cohomology it sends ξ to x↦p₂,*(ξ∪p₁*x), using the coefficient pairing. Under this identification a rational type-(0,0) tensor is a Hodge morphism; a tensor fixed in every étale realization gives G_{F_Σ}-equivariant maps for every ℓ. No assertion that every Hodge class is algebraic is used.

stages.title: The hermitian exterior construction
stages.description: Targets: Hermitian volume: Let E/F be quadratic number fields, H a nondegenerate hermitian form on an n-dimensional right E-space U, conjugate-linear in the first argument, and d_U:∧^n_E U≅E. On exterior powers use the determinant pairing. For w=d_U⁻¹(1), define vol(H,d_U)=H_top(w,w)∈F×. Replacing d_U by αd_U multiplies volume by N_{E/F}(α)⁻¹. The determinant norm identity: For H nondegenerate of dimension n over E/F and g∈GU_E(H) of multiplier ν, N_{E/F}(det_E g)=ν^n. On ∧^r_E U the determinant hermitian pairing has multiplier ν^r. The semilinear exterior operator: For dim_E U=4 and d_U as in volume, let φ:U→U∨ be the conjugate-linear map defined by H, ι:∧²U∨→(∧²U)∨ the determinant dual pairing, and ψ:∧²U→(∧²U)∨ the symmetric perfect wedge pairing followed by d_U. Define L=ψ⁻¹ι(∧²φ). Then L(xα)=L(x)bar α. If an orthogonal basis has coefficients a₁,…,a₄ and d_U(e₁₂₃₄)=−1, its images on (e₁₂,e₁₃,e₁₄,e₂₃,e₂₄,e₃₄) are (−a₁a₂e₃₄,a₁a₃e₂₄,−a₁a₄e₂₃,−a₂a₃e₁₄,a₂a₄e₁₃,−a₃a₄e₁₂). The square of the exterior operator: For exterior-star, L²=J·id with J=vol(H,d_U). Thus every diagonal-coordinate square is a₁a₂a₃a₄ when d_U(e₁₂₃₄)=−1. Exterior skew-pairing identities: Choose trace-zero i∈E× and let b=iH_{∧²}. For exterior-star with J=vol, b(Lx,y)=b(Ly,x) and overline(b(Lx,Ly))=−J b(x,y). The second identity follows from the first and L²=J. These are identities for the E-valued skew-hermitian pairing b, before extension to B. The quaternionic exterior space: Put B=E⊕Ej with j²=J=vol(H,d_U), αj=j bar α, and canonical involution *. On ∧²_E U set xj=Lx, giving a rank-three right B-module. With b=iH_{∧²}, set ⟨x,y⟩=b(x,y)−J⁻¹ j b(Lx,y). This is a nondegenerate B-skew-hermitian form. Rescaling d_U gives an isomorphic B-space through the corresponding change of quaternion generator. The carrier B is an existing quaternion algebra; this target supplies its action and form, not another quaternion-algebra foundation. The exceptional exterior isogeny: Let GSU_E(U)={g∈GU_E(U):det_E g=ν(g)²}. The exterior action gives an algebraic F-group isogeny GSU_E(U)→GU_B(∧²U)^0 with kernel μ₂. The multiplier on the target is ν(g)². For general g, L∘∧²g=(ν(g)²/det g)(∧²g)∘L. The identity component and the scheme-theoretic central kernel are part of the statement. The exceptional projective isomorphism: The exterior construction induces an algebraic F-group isomorphism PGU_E(U)≅PGU_B(∧²U)^0. For g, choose β∈E× with β/bar β=ν(g)²/det g and send x to (∧²g)(x)β modulo the central F×. The class is independent of β and of the central E× representative of g. This agrees with exceptional-isogeny when det g=ν(g)².

stages.title: Block restrictions of the exceptional maps
stages.description: Targets: Quaternionic hermitian planes: For E/F quadratic embedded in B_i, write B_i=E⊕Ej_i with j_i²=J_i. On U_i=B_i as a right E-plane put H_i(a+j_i b,c+j_i d)=bar a c−J_i bar b d. Left-right multiplication x↦βxα⁻¹ identifies GU_E(U_i) with (B_i××E×)/diag F×; its multiplier is Nrd(β)/N(α), and determinant Nrd(β)α⁻². For a general orthogonal plane diag(a₁,a₂) with top trivialization one, the analogous semilinear map has L₁e₁=−a₁e₂, L₁e₂=a₂e₁, square −a₁a₂; its pairing identity has the opposite symmetry from the four-dimensional case. The two-plane exterior decomposition: For U=U₁⊥U₂ with dim_E U_i=2, decompose ∧²U into W=U₁⊗_E U₂ and W₀=∧²U₁⊕∧²U₂ through the ordered wedge inclusions. The operator L preserves both summands, so they have B-ranks two and one and form an orthogonal decomposition of the quaternionic exterior space. The embedding of the equal-multiplier block group is compatible with this splitting. The block exterior isogeny: Let H=GSU_E(U)∩G(U_E(U₁)×U_E(U₂)), where G means equal similitudes. The exterior isogeny restricts to H→G(U_B(W)×U_B(W₀))^0, a central algebraic isogeny with kernel μ₂. Its source and target have dimension eight. The projective block isomorphism: The exceptional projective map restricts to G(U_E(U₁)×U_E(U₂))/E×≅G(U_B(W)×U_B(W₀))^0/F×. For U_i=B_i, write g=([b₁,α₁],[b₂,α₂]) with equal multipliers. Its image is [[b₁,b₂],Nrd(b₁)α₁⁻¹α₂]; this also equals the expression using det(g₁)α₁α₂. The quotient of B₁××B₂× uses t↦(t,t⁻¹). The quaternionic block groups: For the two-plane exterior construction with B_i as above, GU_B(W)^0≅(B₁××B₂×)/{(t,t⁻¹)}, with multiplier Nrd(b₁)Nrd(b₂), and GU_B(W₀)^0≅E× with multiplier N_{E/F}. The second assertion is about the identity component; the full rank-one group also has an involution-normalizer component. The explicit quaternion tensor model: For U=B₁⊥B₂ and ordered E-basis (1,j₁,1,j₂), H has diagonal (1,−J₁,1,−J₂) and J=J₁J₂. On W in order (e₁₃,e₂₃,e₁₄,e₂₄), L sends those vectors to (e₂₄,J₁e₁₄,J₂e₂₃,J₁J₂e₁₃). The E-hermitian form on W is diag(1,−J₁,−J₂,J₁J₂), and [B]=[B₁]+[B₂]. This identifies the exterior block with the quaternion tensor model used for periods. The three-plus-one restriction: If U=U₃⊥U₄ has dimensions three and one, put W=U₃⊗_E U₄, embedded as the mixed wedge summand. The B-action identifies the quaternionic exterior space with W⊗_E B; its skew form extends the E-skew form on W. The exceptional map restricts to G(U_E(U₃)×U_E(U₄))/E×≅GU_E(W)/F×. This is the bounded additional restriction comparison routed to this roadmap; the final theta construction uses the two-plus-two restriction. The exceptional group diagram: Write U=B₁⊥B₂, U~=GU_E(U), H~=G(U_E(B₁)×U_E(B₂)), G~=GU_B(∧²U)^0, and H~_B=G(U_B(W)×U_B(W₀))^0. Form the inclusions H~→U~, H~_B→G~, central quotients U~/E× and G~/F×, and the projective exceptional isomorphisms. Under block-groups write H~_B={(g,α)∈G×E×:ν(g)=Nα}, G=(B₁××B₂×)/anti F×. The diagram commutes as algebraic groups before restriction of scalars to Q.

stages.title: Local models, weights and cohomological theta modules
stages.description: Targets: Local quadratic models: Localize the exterior construction at a characteristic-zero local field, allowing quadratic étale E. When B is split choose the paper’s matrix units and a primitive idempotent e. Imported Morita transfer of forms identifies a skew-hermitian B-space X of rank m with the quadratic F-space X†=Xe of dimension 2m and GU_B(X)^0 with GSO(X†). For the exterior space at real places, the signatures are (4,2) above Σ and (0,6) elsewhere; for W they are (2,2) and (0,4), and for W₀ (2,0) and (0,2). The tensor symplectic space and Weil splittings must agree under Morita, not just the abstract groups. The split exceptional torus map: For the split local model of §6.2, parametrize the unitary maximal torus by (t₁,t₂,ν)∈E××E××F×, with central z represented by (z,z,Nz). Parametrize the quadratic torus by (s₁,s₂,α)∈F××F××E×, modulo its center (z,z,z), z∈F×. The exceptional map is (t₁,t₂,ν)↦(N(t₁t₂),νN(t₁),νt₁bar t₂) modulo that center. The real exceptional torus map: For the real maximal compact tori of §6.3 write z_i=y_i² with z_i,y_i∈C¹. In projective coordinates the map sends (diag(z₁,z₂,z₃,z₄),r) to (y₁y₃/(y₂y₄), y₁y₄/(y₂y₃), y₁y₂/(y₃y₄), r²) modulo the real scalar center. Changing any square root changes the triple by a common central sign, so the projective result is well-defined. The exceptional weight map: On the integral lattice {(l₁,l₂,l₃)∈Z³:l₁+l₂+l₃ is even}, pullback of characters is (l₁,l₂,l₃)↦((l₁+l₂+l₃)/2,(−l₁−l₂+l₃)/2,(l₁−l₂−l₃)/2,(−l₁+l₂−l₃)/2). The four coordinates sum to zero. Its inverse on the sum-zero lattice is (k₁,k₂,k₃,k₄)↦(k₁+k₃,k₁+k₄,k₁+k₂). The cohomological theta module: For even k≥2 the real theta lift from SL₂(R) of the antiholomorphic discrete series D⁻_{k+1} to O(4,2) restricts to A_{q₁}(k−2,0,0) on SO(4,2)^0. Its lowest K-type is (k,0,0), and cohomology with harmonic coefficient H^{k−2} has dimensions one in (1,1) and (3,3), two in (2,2), and zero elsewhere. The holomorphic D⁺_{k+1} gives the holomorphic q₀ module. At O(0,6) the holomorphic lift is the compact representation of highest weight (k−2,0,0), while the antiholomorphic lift vanishes.

stages.title: Harmonic Schwartz forms
stages.description: Targets: Harmonic symmetric tensors: For a nondegenerate real quadratic space X of signature (p,q), let H^ℓX be the kernel of contraction C:Sym^ℓX_C→Sym^{ℓ−2}X_C, C(v₁…v_ℓ)=Σ_{i<j}(v_i,v_j)∏_{r≠i,j}v_r, and C=0 for ℓ<2. Equip Sym^ℓ with the bilinear pairing Σ_{σ∈S_ℓ}∏_i(v_i,w_{σi}), with no division by ℓ!. Use the canonical orthogonal projection Sym^ℓ→H^ℓ from the harmonic decomposition. The polynomial Fock comparison: For the real quadratic model and ψ(x)=exp(2πix), identify the polynomial-times-Gaussian subspace of the Schrödinger model with C[z₁,…,z_m], sending φ₀(x)=exp(−πΣx_i²) to one. On a positive coordinate i, creation x_i−(2π)⁻¹∂_i corresponds to (2πi)⁻¹z_i and annihilation x_i+(2π)⁻¹∂_i to 2i∂/∂z_i. On a negative coordinate j the corresponding operators are −(2πi)⁻¹z_j and −2i∂/∂z_j. These are the four conventions of (8.2); the comparison does not identify all Schwartz functions with polynomials. Harmonic Schwartz forms: Let p,q be nonnegative even integers, p+q=m, and ℓ≥0. For p>0 define φ_{q,ℓ}=(4πi)^{−(q+ℓ)}Σ_{α∈{1,…,p}^q,β∈{1,…,p}^ℓ} z_αz_β⊗ω_α⊗e_β in the Fock model, where ω_α=ω_{α₁,p+1}∧…∧ω_{α_q,p+q}. Project the symmetric coefficient to H^ℓX to get φ′_{q,ℓ}. It is K-invariant, closed for relative Lie algebra cohomology and has K′ weight ℓ+m/2. For p=0 use φ_ℓ=(4πi)^{−ℓ}Σ_{β∈{1,…,m}^ℓ}z_β⊗e_β and its harmonic projection; it is G-invariant and has weight −ℓ−m/2. The first formula includes the source’s factor 2^{−q/2} relative to the original Funke–Millson normalization. The harmonic restriction map: In the six-dimensional quadratic model take X=span(e₁,e₂,e₅,e₆), X₀=span(e₃,e₄). Compose H^ℓ(X⊕X₀)⊂Sym^ℓ(X⊕X₀)→Sym^ℓX→H^ℓX; this is an O(X)-equivariant retraction of the harmonic inclusion. For relative forms also project the cotangent exterior factor. Writing r for symmetric restriction and P for harmonic projection, the diagram in Proposition 8.1 means P_X∘r=harmRestrict∘P_{X⊕X₀}; raw restriction need not preserve harmonic tensors. The noncompact Schwartz restriction formula: For signature (4,2), normalize ω₁₅∧ω₂₅∧ω₁₆∧ω₂₆↦1. Let ω^ε=(ω₁₅+εiω₂₅)∧(ω₁₆+εiω₂₆) and v^ε=(e₁+εie₂)^ℓ/ℓ!, ε=±1. Contract the restricted φ′_{2,ℓ} using wedge with ω^ε and the bilinear coefficient pairing. The resulting Schwartz function is (x₁+εix₂)^{ℓ+2}φ₀(x). The compact Schwartz restriction formula: For signature (0,6), with the same X and v^ε=(e₁+εie₂)^ℓ/ℓ!, coefficient contraction of the restricted compact φ′_ℓ is (−1)^ℓ(x₁+εix₂)^ℓφ₀(x). The application has ℓ=k_v−2 even, but the comparison retains the sign for arbitrary ℓ.

stages.title: Shimura data, coefficients and component characters
stages.description: Targets: The Shimura diagram: Apply Res_{F/Q} to group-diagram. At v∈Σ take h_U(z)=diag(z,z,bar z,bar z) in the unitary realization, with block-plane h_i(z)=diag(z,bar z); outside Σ use the identity. On the quaternionic exterior realization use h_B(z)=diag(z²,zbar z,zbar z) in the paper’s B-basis. The projective maps identify these data and the block arrows are datum morphisms. Their reflex field is F_Σ; the block products and central quotients are taken with their specified data, not arbitrary Shimura data on isomorphic abstract groups. The strict Deligne-data assertion here uses d>0. For d=0 interpret the construction on finite compact Shimura sets with the trivial cocharacter and constant canonical models, as specified in JL.0; the final rank-one correspondence is immediate in this case. The component torus: For H~_B in group-diagram its derived group is (B₁¹×B₂¹)/μ₂ and its abelian quotient is T={([t₁,t₂],α):t₁t₂=Nα}, where (t₁,t₂) is modulo (t,t⁻¹). Its center is Z={(t,α):t²=Nα}, mapping to T by (t,α)↦([t²,1],α)=([t,t],α). The induced Shimura morphism Sh_{H~_B}→Sh_T defines pullback of component functions. It is not asserted to identify the sets of connected components. The component character class: Let η be a finite-order Hecke character of A_E×/E×A_F×, with trivial archimedean component. On T put η_T([t₁,t₂],α)=η((t₁t₂)⁻¹α)=η(α). Its pullback on Z is η(t⁻¹α). The locally constant automorphic character on Sh_T pulls back to c_η∈H⁰(Sh_{H~_B},Q(η)). Use a sufficiently small finite level where η is trivial on the level subgroup. Rational harmonic coefficients: Put ℓ_v=k_v−2. The harmonic representation H^{ℓ_v} on the real quadratic model extends to its connected similitude group by ν^{−ℓ_v/2}; since ℓ_v is even this is algebraic with trivial center. The exterior weight comparison identifies its pullback with the four-dimensional unitary representation of highest weight ((k_v−2)/2,(k_v−2)/2,−(k_v−2)/2,−(k_v−2)/2) in the Borel order of §11.3. The resulting global coefficient has a Q(k)-form unique up to homothety. Its block restriction has a rational equivariant projection to τ_k∨⊠τ_k∨.

stages.title: Quaternionic theta transfer and near equivalence
stages.description: Targets: Toric theta lifting and automorphic induction: Let B/F be quaternion division and split at all real places, E/F CM embedded in B, and η a finite-order Hecke character of E×∖A_E× trivial on A_F×. If η_v does not factor through N_{E_v/F_v} at every place where B is ramified, its theta lift from E× to B× is nonzero, irreducible and is the B× transfer of AI_{E/F}(η). The similitude lift is first defined on the norm-multiplier subgroup H_N^+ and extended by zero to its rational saturation when required. Throughout this packet θ_IP(f) integrates Θ(g,h)f(h), without complex conjugation. Relative to MP.5/global-theta-lift, θ_IP(f)=θ_MP(bar f); at the representation level use θ_MP(bar τ). The corresponding local convention takes the maximal τ∨-isotypic oscillator quotient. Quaternionic product theta lifting: Let B=B₁·B₂ be the division quaternion algebra, and let σ_i be irreducible unitary automorphic representations of B_i× with the same central character, for which the cuspidal JL transfers π_i exist. The theta lift from (B₁××B₂×)/anti F× to B× is zero unless π₁≅π₂; when they agree it is the nonzero transfer π_B of that representation. Its local archimedean components and central character use the fixed Weil splitting. Throughout this packet θ_IP(f) integrates Θ(g,h)f(h), without complex conjugation. Relative to MP.5/global-theta-lift, θ_IP(f)=θ_MP(bar f); at the representation level use θ_MP(bar τ). The corresponding local convention takes the maximal τ∨-isotypic oscillator quotient. The backward-lift doubling point: In the anisotropic rank-three quaternionic setup of Proposition 9.5, use the doubled space and I_v(s) with Levi transformation |Nrd(a)|^(s+5/2). Put a_v(s)=ζ_v(2s)ζ_v(2s−2)ζ_v(2s−4) and b_v(s)=ζ_v(2s+1)ζ_v(2s+3)ζ_v(2s+5). The normalized intertwiner M_v*(s)=(b_v(s)/a_v(s))M_v(s):I_v(s)→I_v(−s) is holomorphic for Re(s)≥0 and has image R(W_v)⊂I_v(−3/2) at s=3/2. For each v there exist a holomorphic section and matrix-coefficient vectors for which the unnormalized local doubling integral Z_v(s) is holomorphic and nonzero at 3/2; no holomorphy for all data is asserted. For normalized unramified data the global factor is L^S(s+1/2,ad τ⊗ξ_E)ζ^S(s+3/2)ζ^S(s+1/2)ζ^S(s−1/2)/[ζ^S(2s+1)ζ^S(2s+3)ζ^S(2s+5)], multiplied by ∏_{v∈S}Z_v(s). Suitable data give a nonzero simple residue at s=3/2. Nonvanishing of the backward lift: Let E/F be quadratic embedded in a division quaternion algebra B split at infinity. Let X be a rank-three skew-hermitian B-space with U(X) F-anisotropic, G=GU_B(X)^0, and H_N^+={h∈B×(A_F):Nrd(h)∈N(A_E×)}. Let τ be an irreducible unitary automorphic representation of H_N^+ whose forward theta lift Π to G is nonzero and cuspidal. If Π′ is an irreducible unitary automorphic representation of G nearly equivalent to Π, then θ_IP(bar Π′) to H_N^+ is nonzero. The proof uses the nonzero residue of the doubled integral at s=3/2 and the Siegel–Weil identity with the normalization of §9.5. Throughout this packet θ_IP(f) integrates Θ(g,h)f(h), without complex conjugation. Relative to MP.5/global-theta-lift, θ_IP(f)=θ_MP(bar f); at the representation level use θ_MP(bar τ). The corresponding local convention takes the maximal τ∨-isotypic oscillator quotient. Near-equivalence rigidity of theta lifts: Under the hypotheses of backward-lift, every irreducible unitary automorphic Π′ of G nearly equivalent to θ_IP(τ) is θ_IP(τ′) for an irreducible unitary automorphic representation τ′ of H_N^+ nearly equivalent to τ. Take τ′=bar θ_IP(bar Π′), using backward nonvanishing, local Howe duality and unramified parameter recovery. The assertion concerns these rank-three anisotropic lifts, not strong multiplicity one for all unitary automorphic representations or a lift from the full group B×(A_F).

stages.title: Simultaneous nonvanishing of restricted theta classes
stages.description: Targets: Global theta data: In the distinct-algebra case of JL.0 choose a common CM subfield E⊂B_i, write B_i=E⊕Ej_i, and take the spaces and groups of the exceptional diagram. Put H=B×, H_N^+={h∈H(A_F):Nrd(h)∈N(A_E×)}, and H_∞^+={h:Nrd(h_v)>0 for every real v}. These subgroups serve different purposes. Set ℓ_v=k_v−2 and take the Schwartz form φ′_{2,ℓ_v} at v∈Σ and φ′_{ℓ_v} elsewhere, with a pure-tensor finite Schwartz vector. For an irreducible unitary automorphic τ on H_N^+ use central character ξ_E, antiholomorphic minimal type of weight k_v+1 at Σ and holomorphic type outside Σ. The exterior isometry group is F-anisotropic: because d<n, at least one real localization is compact O(0,6), which excludes an F-split torus. Its adelic quotient modulo the center is compact. All theta-integral convergence claims use this fact. Throughout this packet θ_IP(f) integrates Θ(g,h)f(h), without complex conjugation. Relative to MP.5/global-theta-lift, θ_IP(f)=θ_MP(bar f); at the representation level use θ_MP(bar τ). The corresponding local convention takes the maximal τ∨-isotypic oscillator quotient. The theta cohomology class: For global-theta-data and a minimal-type vector φ∈τ, theta lifting the tensor-valued Schwartz form gives a closed 2d-form θ_{φ~}(φ) on the quaternionic exterior Shimura variety, with the harmonic coefficient of JL.5. The central transformation rule in Proposition A.1 cancels τ’s ξ_E character, so the form has trivial central character. Denote its cohomology class by ξ_τ. Dependence on the finite Schwartz vector and φ is linear with the convention for conjugation fixed in the theta integral. Explicitly its integrand is Θ(g,h)φ(h), so it is linear in φ; the MP.5 supplier is applied to bar φ to match its conjugated-input convention. Central projection and normalized descent: Restrict ξ_τ to H~_B. For the center Z={(z,α):z²=Nα}, use p(z,α)=z⁻¹α∈E¹ and project by the normalized integral ∫_{Z(G~)(A)Z(F)∖Z(A)} ξ_τ(zg)(η∘p)(z)dz, with quotient volume one. Multiply the resulting η⁻¹-equivariant form by c_η. For g∈G(A)^+ choose α_g with Nα_g=ν(g) and evaluate at (g,α_g), multiplied by η(α_g). This is independent of α_g. Descend by normalized trace, extend by zero off G(F)G(A)^+, and average over K using volume one. The restricted theta seesaw: For the projected and descended form and the vectors f₁^ε⊠f₂^ε of Proposition 10.1, pairing against their coefficient and differential factors equals the scalar theta integral of Lemma 10.2. The compatible-splitting seesaw rewrites it as the triple product integral over H_N^+: θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε)·θ_{φ₀}(η)·φ. Use the central quotient and measures of §10.4, with absolute convergence from the compact quotient and cusp input. The seesaw is equation (10.7), p. 72; equation (10.8) is a later K-type identity. The simultaneous sign theta vectors: For each ε∈{±1}^{Σ∞}, choose the archimedean Schwartz factor (x₁+ε_vi x₂)^{k_v}φ₀ above Σ and (x₁+ε_vi x₂)^{k_v−2}φ₀ elsewhere. For the Proposition 10.1 vectors, finite Schwartz data can be chosen once so that θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) is nonzero for every ε and belongs to π_B, of minimal weights +k_v at Σ and −k_v elsewhere. The archimedean Whittaker coefficient is nonzero and its ε-dependence disappears for the even exponents. Rescale the f^ε so these lifts agree as one nonzero automorphic form. Moving theta support to the norm subgroup: Assume there is a finite place v₀ at which E/F is ramified, B₁ and B₂ are split, and the finite level is hyperspecial. For the common nonzero sign theta form of sign-theta, its restriction to H_N^+ is nonzero after the permitted translation. Use a unit at v₀ outside the local norm group and the block-group element whose image fixes the prescribed hyperspecial vectors to exchange the two norm-support cosets. The auxiliary finite-order character: There exists a finite-order η of A_E×/E×A_F×, trivial at infinity, whose local component does not factor through the norm at every finite place ramified in B. Choose local characters χ_v on E_v¹ with χ_v²≠1, extend their product to A_E¹/E¹, and define η(x)=χ(x/bar x). Keep the square condition: merely choosing χ_v nontrivial need not suffice. The auxiliary toric theta vector: For auxiliary-character there is finite Schwartz data φ₀ with archimedean Gaussian factors, normalized by φ₀,v(0)=1, such that θ_{φ₀}(η) is nonzero on H_N^+. Its real weights are +1 at v∈Σ and −1 elsewhere, with the scalar quadratic-space conventions fixed by the block decomposition. The minimal triple-product type: If the pointwise product θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε)θ_{φ₀}(η) is nonzero, then at each real place it generates the minimal discrete-series type of weight k_v+1: holomorphic at Σ and antiholomorphic outside Σ. Thus its contragredient is the archimedean type required for τ in global-theta-data. Simultaneous nonvanishing of the restriction: Let f₁^ε⊠f₂^ε have opposite archimedean weights ±k_v above Σ and ±(k_v−2) elsewhere, the same finite vector for all ε, and be K-fixed. Under the v₀ hypothesis of norm-support, there is a single choice of τ, φ, η and Schwartz data for which the descended theta class pairs nontrivially with every one of these 2^n sign vectors. The finite data and auxiliary representation are common to all signs.

stages.title: The unitary eigenspace and its Hodge type
stages.description: Targets: The theta Arthur parameter: Choose an irreducible unitary cuspidal σ on GL₂(A_F), with central character ξ_E, whose B× Jacquet–Langlands transfer restricts to H_N^+ with a constituent τ. Its quadratic base change σ_E is independent of this choice and is conjugate-orthogonal. The subgroup representation τ itself is not an input to the usual GL₂ transfer. If cuspidal, it gives the elliptic U(4) parameter ψ=σ_E⊠Sym¹; if noncuspidal, write σ_E=χ⊞χ⁻¹, where χ is conjugate-orthogonal and χ²≠1, and interpret ψ as the corresponding sum of two simple blocks. The sign follows from As⁺∘BC=Sym²⊕(∧²⊗ξ_E), so L(s,As⁺σ_E)=L(s,Sym²σ)ζ_F(s). This σ is the auxiliary central-character-ξ_E representation, distinct from the initial central-character-one π. The U(2,2) Adams–Johnson packet: For even k≥2 consider ψ∞=(χ_{k/2}⊠Sym¹)⊕(χ_{−k/2}⊠Sym¹) and coefficient highest weight λ=(k/2−1,k/2−1,−k/2+1,−k/2+1). Its packet on U(2,2) has q₀,q₁,q₂ representatives indexed by 1,(23),(13)(24). With the dual coefficient, q₀ has cohomology of dimension one in (4,0), q₁ dimensions one, two, one in (1,1),(2,2),(3,3), and q₂ dimension one in (0,4); every other bidegree is zero. The identification with the relevant local Arthur packet is imported with its precise real-classification hypotheses. The negative-similitude involution: The real similitude δ exchanging the two signature blocks of U(2,2), with multiplier −1, acts on the packet by interchanging q₀ and q₂ and preserving q₁. Thus passing from the unitary group to the full relevant real similitude group does not introduce a different degree-two type. The rational theta Hecke space: Let Π=θ(τ) on the exterior quaternionic group and transport it through the central/projective diagram to the unitary group with coefficient V_k. For sufficiently large S and small level K, let I be the kernel of the away-S rational Hecke action on Π_f^K. The Q(k)-space H^{2d}(Sh_K,V_k)[I] complexifies to the sum of all coefficient-conjugate Π^σ eigenspaces, not only one chosen complex eigenspace. Each summand has the Matsushima decomposition over representations nearly equivalent to Π^σ. Degree selection in the theta eigenspace: In degree 2d of hecke-eigenspace, each v∈Σ contributes degree two and the q₁ module, while every real place outside Σ contributes degree zero. Thus the relative cochain bidegree is (d,d). One proof uses the packet and negative-similitude calculation. A second uses near-equivalence rigidity and the explicit archimedean theta module, as in Remark 11.5; it avoids depending on the global packet classification. This is a relative-cochain statement; actual Hodge types require hodge-weight-comparison. Coefficient and cochain Hodge weights: For the U(2,2) coefficient at even k≥2, use the standard geometric coefficient with fiber weight 2k−4 and the six Kostant representatives of Proposition 11.6. The cochain positions (0,4),(1,1),(2,2),(2,2),(3,3),(4,0) have actual untwisted Hodge types (0,2k),(k−1,k−1),(k,k),(k,k),(k+1,k+1),(2k,0). Add (2−k,2−k) for the unitary coefficient normalization. In particular the cochain (1,1) term has actual type (1,1) after normalization, for every k. This calculation compares the homogeneous variation and its automorphic unitary normalization. Purity of the theta Hecke space: The degree-2d Π^S eigenspace on the unitary Shimura variety, and its counterpart on the quaternionic exterior variety, is purely of actual Hodge type (d,d). The same holds for every coefficient conjugate in hecke-eigenspace. After twist (d), the entire Q(k)-rational Hecke space is type (0,0). This uses the coefficient-normalized degree selection, not an identification of relative cochain indices with Hodge indices in general.

stages.title: The conditional Galois calculation
stages.description: Targets: The cocharacter representation: For the unitary similitude group over F use dual group GL₄×G_m with nontrivial Gal(E/F) action (g,ν)↦(θ₄(g),νdet g). Let r=(∧²std⊗ν)∨, normalized by the cocharacter’s extreme weight −μ. Extend through Gal(E/F) by the unique intertwiner fixing a highest-weight vector. For Res_{F/Q} take r₀=⊗_{v∈Σ}r_v and extend to G_{F_Σ} by the ordinary tensor-permutation action with the prescribed local intertwiners. The tensor factors are not graded objects, so no Koszul signs are introduced. Conditional trivial semisimplification: Assume Kottwitz’s conjectural description in the precise degree-wise form of §11.5 for these unitary similitude Shimura varieties: H^i_et[Π^S]^ss embeds in a finite sum of r_ℓ^{i−4d}(ψ₀), with its fixed cocharacter and coefficient normalization. For ψ=(σ_E⊠Sym¹,1), the twisted degree-2d eigenspace H^{2d}_et[Π^S](d)^ss is trivial under G_{F_Σ}. Indeed the single-factor bottom Arthur weight is V^{−2}=|·|⁻¹; the total weight −2d uses only these lines, and twist (d) cancels the tensor character including its permutation action. Triviality of geometric unipotent extensions: Let k be a number field, ℓ a prime, and W a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-representation of G_k, unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham at v|ℓ. If W^ss is trivial, W is trivial. The special extension group needed is H¹_g(k,Q_ℓ)=0: local class field theory identifies a de Rham extension of the trivial representation by itself at v|ℓ with a homomorphism k_v×/O_v×→Q_ℓ; away from ℓ every continuous additive Q_ℓ-character is unramified. The global class factors through the finite ideal class group and vanishes. Induct on a filtration with trivial quotients. Conditional trivial Galois action: Under the Kottwitz hypothesis of galois-semisimplification, the full degree-2d étale Π^S eigenspace after twist (d) has trivial G_{F_Σ}-action for every ℓ. Apply unipotent-splitting to the geometric cohomology representation, and transport the conclusion to the quaternionic exterior group and to every coefficient-conjugate summand of hecke-eigenspace.

stages.title: Rational descent and the main theorems
stages.description: Targets: The auxiliary Hilbert representation: The τ chosen by all-sign-nonvanishing comes from a cohomological cuspidal GL₂(A_F) representation obtained from a holomorphic Hilbert modular form of weights k_v+1 and an odd algebraic norm weight r, with finite central character ξ_E. After the prescribed norm twist and JL transfer to B×, its restriction contains the required source representation: antiholomorphic above Σ and holomorphic outside Σ. Track restriction first to the positive-infinity subgroup and then to the norm subgroup; do not identify these two subgroups. The common CM field with a support place: For distinct B₁,B₂ choose a finite place v₀ outside their ramification and the prescribed finite bad set, and a CM quadratic E/F ramified at v₀, nonsplit at every finite place ramified in either B_i. Then E embeds into both B_i, and sufficiently small levels can be chosen hyperspecial at v₀ while preserving the desired finite automorphic vectors. This supplies the additional local hypothesis used in Proposition 10.1. The realization-compatible restriction map: For a fixed finite level on the exterior variety and a component parameter c, define Res_c:H^{2d}(Sh_{G~},V~)(d)→V₁⊗_L V₂(d)≅Hom_L(V₁,V₂). In order: pull back to the block subgroup; apply the rational harmonic coefficient projection; multiply by c; take the normalized central trace to the projective quaternionic block group; average at a compatible level; pull back from G to the product B₁××B₂×; apply the L-rational π₁⊠π₂ projector; contract the chosen L-rational finite representation vectors. The map is Q(k)-linear in the source and Q-linear in c, with target coefficients L. Its construction is in compatible Betti/étale realizations over F_Σ whenever c is Galois invariant. Invertibility of the theta correspondence: There is complex auxiliary data for which Res_{c_η}(ξ_τ(d)):V₁,C→V₂,C is an isomorphism. In the tensor sign bases it has a nonzero entry on each matching line and no other entries: the coefficient pairings and restriction fix the individual archimedean signs, and all-sign-nonvanishing makes each allowed entry nonzero. Thus its rank is 2^d. Nonzero of one matrix coefficient would not suffice. Galois-invariant component parameters: At a fixed finite level let W_Q=H⁰(Sh_{H~_B},Q)^{G_{F_Σ}}, where the action is the actual finite permutation action on components. For the character η of auxiliary-character, c_η belongs to W_Q⊗Q(η). To prove this, factor the torus datum cocharacter through j:Res_{F/Q}G_m→T, j(s)=([s,s],s). Functoriality of the reflex norm places its finite-idele image in j(A_{F,f}×). Since η_T(j(s))=η(s⁻¹)=1, torus reciprocity fixes c_η; pullback is equivariant. Invariants commute with scalar extension because this is a finite permutation representation. No triviality of the entire component action is asserted. Rational determinant descent: Let H be the Q(k)-rational Hecke space of hecke-eigenspace and W_Q the invariant component space of component-galois-invariants. Fix L-rational finite representation parameters as in restriction-correspondence. The determinant of Res_c(x) is a polynomial in coordinates of x∈H and c∈W_Q, with coefficients in L. Complex-invertibility and c_η∈W_Q⊗C give a complex point where it is nonzero. Since Q(k) and Q are infinite, choose x∈H and c∈W_Q at which it remains nonzero, treating the two parameter blocks successively. The resulting tensor ξ₀ has coefficients L, is Hodge by purity of every conjugate summand, and is invertible.  Hodge classes for Jacquet–Langlands: For Jacquet–Langlands Hodge data there exists ξ₀∈V₁⊗_L V₂(d) of Hodge type (0,0) whose correspondence operator is an isomorphism V₁≅V₂ of L-Hodge structures. This is unconditional. It is the assertion of Theorem 12.4(i), hence Theorem 3.2(i); the equal-algebra branch is supplied by the identity correspondence. The statement constructs a Hodge class, without claiming it is an algebraic cycle or an absolute Hodge class. Conditional Hodge–Tate correspondence: Assume the unitary-similitude Kottwitz conjecture in galois-semisimplification. The ξ₀ of main-hodge can be chosen in HT(V₁⊗_L V₂(d)): it is a rational Hodge tensor whose image is G_{F_Σ}-fixed in every ℓ-adic realization. Its induced isomorphisms V₁⊗Q_ℓ≅V₂⊗Q_ℓ are G_{F_Σ}-equivariant simultaneously for all rational primes ℓ. Here HT is the compatible-realization notion of §12.1, not the local p-adic Hodge–Tate condition alone. The rational weight-two correspondence: When all k_v=2 and Q(π)=Q, the local systems are constant and the final class is represented in the π₁⊠π₂ summand of H^{2d}(X₁×X₂,Q)(d) at suitable finite levels. The map x↦p₂,*(ξ₀∪p₁*x) is an isomorphism of the degree-d rational Hodge multiplicity spaces. Under the explicit Kottwitz hypothesis it induces G_{F_Σ}-equivariant isomorphisms in all ℓ-adic realizations. Finite-level representation factors are retained when translating from multiplicity spaces to the full isotypic summands.
